Take 1 teaspoon of black seed oil every morning to help reduce burning, red cheeks in 30 days.

videos.title: Längre, rakare och lättare. Sträck ut den bakre armen - Järnslag
videos.channel: Enklare & Bättre golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Längre, rakare och lättare. Sträck ut den bakre armen - Järnslag Att sträcka ut den bakre armen med kraft ger dig längd i alla slag men timingen ger dig bättre kontroll. Såhär vet du om du har gjort det rätt. 

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro - Sträck ut i rätt tid. 
1:00 Att förstå hur slaget påverkas är nyckeln till framgång. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Sam Bennett had his second hat trick of the season with Sandis Vilmanis getting the game-winner late in the third. 

The line of Bennett, Vilmanis, and Eetu Luostarinen had all four goals and three assists. 

Jacob Markstrom made 17 saves. 

The Panthers are off until hosting the Senators on Wednesday.

Choosing nutrient-dense whole foods is an important step toward improving your daily nutrition. From fermented foods for gut health to omega-3-rich fish, leafy greens, quality protein, selenium-rich nuts, and healthy fats, these foods offer a variety of nutrients your body needs.

videos.title: How my speed training going. Better than expected…
videos.channel: Easier & Better golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
How my speed training going. Better than expected… In spite being sick for a few days my speed training is going better than expected. This is a summary of today’s session.

golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro -How is my swing speed training going?
1:00 Today it feels easy
7:00 A new high score

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are missleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice.

5 Daily Habits That Help Protect You From Cancer and Disease | Dr. Mandell Every single day, your body is exposed to invisible forces that can damage your cells, accelerate aging, and contribute to serious diseases, including cancer, heart disease, and diabetes. One of these forces is oxidative stress, which occurs when harmful levels of free radicals overwhelm your body's natural antioxidant defenses. But here's the fascinating part: the choices you make every day can influence how well your body protects itself! In this powerful video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how oxidative stress affects your cells, DNA, blood vessels, and organs, and why simple daily habits can make a tremendous difference in your long-term health. Discover how antioxidant-rich foods such as blueberries, spinach, broccoli, nuts, seeds, and green tea support cellular health, how omega-3 fatty acids contribute to cardiovascular wellness, and why quality sleep, regular exercise, hydration, and stress management are essential for maintaining a healthier body. You'll also learn how smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, poor dietary habits, and inadequate sleep can contribute to inflammation and cellular damage. Think of your body like a health bank account: every healthy choice is a deposit toward your future, while unhealthy habits can gradually drain your reserves. Scientific research supports the connection between healthy lifestyle patterns and lower risks of several chronic diseases, including certain cancers. No single food or habit guarantees cancer prevention, but the choices you make consistently can help reduce important risk factors. Start making those healthy deposits today, because your health is your greatest wealth! Please share this important information with your friends and loved ones, and make it a great day! — Dr. Alan Mandell, DC, motivationaldoc

videos.title: The AI Battle of 2026: Which Model Is Actually Smarter?
videos.summary_source_text:
The AI Battle of 2026: Which Model Is Actually Smarter? OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra has officially challenged Claude Fable 5.2, and the independent benchmarks make this AI intelligence race far more complicated than anyone expected.

Released on November 17, 2026, GPT-6.2 Astra scores 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, compared to Claude Fable 5.2's 65. OpenAI has erased more than half of its previous intelligence gap in a single update. Meanwhile, Epoch AI's independent Capabilities Index puts both models at approximately 174.

But that's where things get interesting.

On ARC-AGI-3, Claude Fable 5.2 beats GPT-6.2 Astra by 10.9 percentage points under the Standard harness. Change the evaluation harness, however, and Astra achieves a perfect 100%, overtaking Claude's 97.7%. The same benchmark produces two completely different winners.

Both models also achieve 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. But does a perfect mathematics score actually prove superior intelligence? We examine benchmark saturation, previously unsolved Erdős problems, reasoning effort, and why increasingly difficult evaluations are necessary.

This video breaks down the independent evidence available as of November 18, 2026, rather than relying exclusively on OpenAI and Anthropic's carefully selected launch demonstrations.

We explore the most important differences between GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, including:

• Artificial Analysis, Epoch AI and Vals AI intelligence rankings
• ARC-AGI-1, ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3 reasoning benchmarks
• FrontierMath and previously open mathematical problems
• Terminal-Bench 4.0 and FrontierCode 2.0 coding performance
• Scientific research and autonomous agent capabilities
• Robotics, interactive 3D environments and engineering simulations
• API pricing, token consumption, reasoning speed and task efficiency
• Million-token context windows and their limitations
• Cybersecurity, deception and AI self-improvement risks
• Independent real-world workplace evaluations

Science is arguably GPT-6.2 Astra's strongest case. OpenAI's new flagship takes first place on the independent Vals Science Index with 68.44%, compared to Claude's 63.74%. Astra also completes that workload faster while consuming significantly fewer tokens.

Then there's the pricing surprise.

Both GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 now cost $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. However, identical token prices do not translate into identical task costs.

On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, Astra averages $4 per task at maximum reasoning effort, while Fable averages $26.54. That difference could become enormously important for businesses deploying autonomous AI agents at scale.

But Claude still has significant advantages, including cheaper cache reads, stronger performance across several coding and knowledge benchmarks, and a substantial lead in Epoch AI's independent workplace research evaluation.

We also examine OpenAI's new demonstrations, including a car suspension simulation, interactive 3D environments, a playable pinball machine and an architectural paper lamp. These are compared with Anthropic's robotic manipulation and electronics design demonstrations, while separating curated successes from independent evidence.

Beyond performance, both models raise serious AI safety questions. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra meets its Critical cybersecurity threshold and High AI self-improvement threshold. We examine its reported deception regressions, evaluation awareness, monitoring limitations and Anthropic's own safety warnings.

And despite both models offering approximately one million tokens of context, we still lack a matched independent evaluation proving which model can reliably retrieve and reason across that entire window.

So, is GPT-6.2 Astra actually smarter than Claude Fable 5.2? Has OpenAI finally caught Anthropic? Or are we reaching a point where intelligence rankings matter less than reliability, efficiency and the specific work these models can accomplish?

The answer depends heavily on what you're measuring — and how you're measuring it.

But that's where things get interesting.

On ARC-AGI-3, Claude Fable 5.2 beats GPT-6.2 Astra by 10.9 percentage points under the Standard harness. Change the evaluation harness, however, and Astra achieves a perfect 100%, overtaking Claude's 97.7%. The same benchmark produces two completely different winners.

Both models also achieve 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. But does a perfect mathematics score actually prove superior intelligence? We examine benchmark saturation, previously unsolved Erdős problems, reasoning effort, and why increasingly difficult evaluations are necessary.

This video breaks down the independent evidence available as of November 18, 2026, rather than relying exclusively on OpenAI and Anthropic's carefully selected launch demonstrations.

We explore the most important differences between GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, including:

• Artificial Analysis, Epoch AI and Vals AI intelligence rankings
• ARC-AGI-1, ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3 reasoning benchmarks
• FrontierMath and previously open mathematical problems
• Terminal-Bench 4.0 and FrontierCode 2.0 coding performance
• Scientific research and autonomous agent capabilities
• Robotics, interactive 3D environments and engineering simulations
• API pricing, token consumption, reasoning speed and task efficiency
• Million-token context windows and their limitations
• Cybersecurity, deception and AI self-improvement risks
• Independent real-world workplace evaluations

Science is arguably GPT-6.2 Astra's strongest case. OpenAI's new flagship takes first place on the independent Vals Science Index with 68.44%, compared to Claude's 63.74%. Astra also completes that workload faster while consuming significantly fewer tokens.

Then there's the pricing surprise.

Both GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 now cost $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. However, identical token prices do not translate into identical task costs.

On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, Astra averages $4 per task at maximum reasoning effort, while Fable averages $26.54. That difference could become enormously important for businesses deploying autonomous AI agents at scale.

But Claude still has significant advantages, including cheaper cache reads, stronger performance across several coding and knowledge benchmarks, and a substantial lead in Epoch AI's independent workplace research evaluation.

We also examine OpenAI's new demonstrations, including a car suspension simulation, interactive 3D environments, a playable pinball machine and an architectural paper lamp. These are compared with Anthropic's robotic manipulation and electronics design demonstrations, while separating curated successes from independent evidence.

Beyond performance, both models raise serious AI safety questions. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra meets its Critical cybersecurity threshold and High AI self-improvement threshold. We examine its reported deception regressions, evaluation awareness, monitoring limitations and Anthropic's own safety warnings.

And despite both models offering approximately one million tokens of context, we still lack a matched independent evaluation proving which model can reliably retrieve and reason across that entire window.

So, is GPT-6.2 Astra actually smarter than Claude Fable 5.2? Has OpenAI finally caught Anthropic? Or are we reaching a point where intelligence rankings matter less than reliability, efficiency and the specific work these models can accomplish?

The answer depends heavily on what you're measuring — and how you're measuring it.

videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra Is Actually AGI! OpenAI just released GPT-6.2 Astra, and the numbers are extraordinary. A nearly 20-percentage-point jump in engineering benchmarks, a 99.8% score in one ARC Prize testing configuration, breakthrough mathematical reasoning, and the first externally deployed OpenAI model officially rated "High" for AI self-improvement.

But does this mean we've finally reached AGI? The independent evidence tells a much more complicated story.

Released on November 17, 2026, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol represent OpenAI's latest push toward autonomous AI agents capable of engineering, scientific research, coding, computer use, and complex professional work.

videos.title: They Die Young - What's Killing Bodybuilders?
videos.summary_source_text:
They Die Young - What's Killing Bodybuilders? In 2018, Shawn Rhoden was crowned Mr. Olympia. Three years later he was dead at 46. Dallas McCarver died at 26. When researchers followed 20,286 competitive bodybuilders, 121 had died, and the deaths had something in common.

In this film: what the largest study of bodybuilder deaths found (European Heart Journal, 2025), what anabolic steroids do to the heart (thickening, stiffening, scarring and broken rhythm), why it's not just steroids (growth hormone, insulin, SARMs), why the week before a show is the most dangerous of all (diuretics, dehydration and potassium), the pressure that drives it, and what any lifter can do now.

This is education, not a diagnosis. If you have ever used performance-enhancing drugs, tell your doctor the truth, and ask about your blood pressure, cholesterol, blood count and a scan of your heart.

Before You Hit Your Irons, Do This For 5 Seconds Struggle with inconsistent ball striking, poor distance or a golf swing that feels harder than it should?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn how one common takeaway fault can ruin your strike, rob you of distance and make the golf swing far less repeatable.

The surprising part is that Danny Maude found the same fault in his own golf swing.

After reviewing more than **400,000 swings** inside the Swing Coach app, this same pattern appeared again and again: golfers heaving, lifting or lunging the club away from the ball instead of allowing the clubhead to move naturally with the body.

A simple drill from coach Andrew Nicholson changed the movement within just a handful of swings.

In this golf lesson you’ll learn:

• How a poor takeaway can ruin ball striking  
• Why golfers sway away from the golf ball  
• How lifting the club makes the backswing harder  
• Why the clubhead needs to move faster early in the backswing  
• How to create a natural lever in the takeaway  
• The split-hand drill that changed Danny Maude’s golf swing  
• How pushing with the lead hand and pulling with the trail hand can organise the backswing  
• Why a better takeaway can improve posture and reduce sway naturally  
• How to make the golf swing feel more effortless and repeatable  

The key idea is not to force your head to stay still or consciously stop yourself swaying.

Instead, change the way the golf club moves at the start.

By creating a lever with the hands, the clubhead can begin to rise naturally as the body turns. That can help the shoulders work on a better arc and allow the whole backswing to organise itself without you trying to control lots of separate positions.

Discover the connection between estrogen, progesterone, and joint pain, plus the surprising causes of referred shoulder pain.

Fascia is the connective tissue that surrounds your muscles and organs. It contains receptors for estrogen and progesterone, which may help explain why frozen shoulder is most common in women between the ages of 40 and 60.

Progesterone begins to decline 8 to 10 years before menopause. During this hormonal shift, the adrenal glands work harder to compensate. They rely on cholesterol, the raw material needed to produce hormones, bile salts, and vitamin D.

Low cholesterol can affect bile production, potentially contributing to bile sludge and gallbladder problems. Irritation involving the phrenic nerve can also cause referred shoulder pain.

Shoulder stiffness and joint pain may be directly related to changes in the fascia as progesterone declines. Hormonal shifts, insufficient cholesterol, and stress on the adrenal glands may all contribute to the problem.

Adequate cholesterol helps provide the raw materials for hormone production during perimenopause and menopause. Vitamin D deficiency may make these problems worse.

To help reduce frozen shoulder and other joint pain after menopause:

1. Increase cholesterol intake.
2. Take 10,000 IU of vitamin D with vitamin K2 and magnesium.
3. Take ox bile or TUDCA.

Corvette ZR1 v Lambo Revuelto v Porsche 911 Turbo S: DRAG RACE We want to say a huge thank you to all the people that made this video possible. Go and follow them!

Corvette ZR1: https://www.instagram.com/itscorvetteeric/
Corvette ZR1: https://www.instagram.com/gmgcarz/

It’s an absolute heavyweight three-way clash on the runway today! 🇺🇸🇮🇹🇩🇪

Mat’s lining up in the hybrid Lamborghini Revuelto to take on the monstrous new Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 and the undefeated launch-control king, the 992.2 Porsche 911 Turbo S! Three completely different engineering philosophies are going head-to-head over the standing quarter mile - so let’s see how the stats stack up before the lights go out!

Starting with the Chevy, the Corvette ZR1 packs a titanic 5.5-litre twin-turbo flat-plane crank V8 producing an outrageous 1,079hp and 1,123Nm of torque! All of that fury is sent exclusively to the rear wheels via an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox, it tips the scales at around 1,765kg and costs around £150,000.

Next up is the Lamborghini Revuelto. Behind the cabin sits a naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V12 paired with three electric motors for a combined 1,015hp and over 1,062Nm of torque. Power goes to all four wheels through an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission, though all that hybrid tech pushes its kerb weight up to around 1,872kg and costs it £454,830.

Finally, we have the facelifted 992.2 Porsche 911 Turbo S - now featuring Porsche’s new T-Hybrid system! It pairs a 3.6-litre flat-six with twin electric turbochargers (eTurbos) and an electric motor integrated into the 8-speed PDK gearbox for a combined 711hp and 800Nm of torque. It’s still down on power compared to its four-figure rivalsm, weighs 1,725kg, and it costs £199,500 but with zero turbo lag and Porsche’s legendary all-wheel-drive launch control, it’s more than capable of pulling off a giant-killing upset!

Will the rear-wheel-drive Chevy’s sheer horsepower prevail, will the V12 hybrid Lambo’s all-wheel-drive traction carry it to victory, or will the Porsche pull off another giant-killing upset? There’s only one way to find out… LET’S RACE! 🏁

videos.title: 20.11.26 - RIFT Training Day
videos.summary_source_text:
20.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Rory McIlroy v Eugenio Chacarra Final Round | 2026 DP World Tour Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Rory McIlroy v Eugenio Chacarra Final Round | 2026 DP World Tour Championship Every shot of Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra from the final round of the 2026 DP World Tour Championship, the closest Race to Dubai race in years.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. There are two key pieces of silverware on offer this week, The DP World Tour Championship and the Harry Vardon Trophy. The battle for the Race to Dubai title comes to an end this week at Jumeirah Golf Club as players vie to end the year as DP World Tour Number One. There are still nine players in the running to end the year at the top of the Ranking. Eugenio Chacarra, the only three time winner this season, tops the standings heading in with a 533.93 point lead over nearest challenger Rory McIlroy, who is seeking to match Colin Montgomerie’s long-standing record of eight Order of Merit titles this week. With Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, US PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier all are still in with a chance of ending the year as the winner of the season-long race.

How Riley Moss' $67M Extension Changes Denver's Roster Outlook | DNVR DRAFT POD The Broncos just locked up Riley Moss — four years, $67 million — and with Pat Surtain II signed through 2029, both starting corner spots are set for years. But left guard is still the open question: Ben Powers is in his final contract year, Kage Casey was drafted to start there in 2027, and a switch now would be both a 2026 fix and a 2027 audition. We break down the Broncos' long-term roster outlook, then the Arch Manning throw debate, Fernando Mendoza's debut ahead of his second start Sunday in Denver, and the latest risers. Join Jake Schwanitz, Henry Chisholm and Andre Simone for all things Denver Broncos, college football and the NFL Draft.

In 13 years between GTA games, has CSU gotten any closer to being a power conference football team? Justin Michael talks about the release of Grand Theft Auto VI and what has changed, as well as what is different about the state of CSU Football since the last game was released in 2013. Justin explores if the Rams are truly any closer to being a power conference football program and gives a few thoughts on the uncertain future. He also previews the Fresno State game and re-highlights just how bad the CSU defense has been this fall. Finally, Justin talks a little hoops and whether the Maui Invitational can provide a spark for the Rams. He also gives an updated Pac-12 power ranking, Week 12 upset picks and more.

videos.title: Hindi - 20.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 20.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

PGA Tour Highlights | Round 2 | The RSM Classic | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 2 of the 2026 The RSM Classic, featuring Michael Thorbjornsen, Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen and John Parry, among others.

The PGA Tour season reaches its conclusion this week at The RSM Classic, with plenty at stake at Sea Island as players make their final push for 2027 status. Only the top 100 in the FedExCup Fall standings will secure full playing privileges, leaving several notable names under pressure. Billy Horschel sits just outside the line at No. 101, while Joel Dahmen, Luke Clanton and Haotong Li face a steep climb from further back. Peter Malnati has an even tougher task at No. 151, knowing only a victory can take him into the top 100. Sami Valimaki returns to defend his title, while five-time major champion Brooks Koepka makes his tournament debut. The Aon Next 10 is also up for grabs, with places 51-60 earning starts in the first two Signature Events of 2027. The lineup also includes the in-form Andrew Novak, Austin Smotherman and Blades Brown as well as Major Champion Brian Harman, the field is stacked and it is set to be a thrilling finale.

videos.title: Ozempic, Wegovy & Mounjaro New FDA Warning! (GLP-1 Drugs)   Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Ozempic, Wegovy & Mounjaro New FDA Warning! (GLP-1 Drugs)   Dr. Mandell Millions of people are taking Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound to lose weight, control blood sugar, and improve their metabolic health. But on November 9, 2026, the FDA announced an important new safety warning involving GLP-1 medications and a rare but serious eye condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss. The condition, known as nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), occurs when the blood supply to the optic nerve becomes insufficient, potentially damaging the nerve responsible for carrying visual information from your eyes to your brain. After reviewing 126 randomized clinical trials involving more than 134,000 participants, the FDA identified a higher occurrence of NAION among patients receiving GLP-1 medications compared with those receiving other treatments or placebo. Although this complication is extremely rare, the findings are important enough that the FDA is requiring updated medication warnings. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the physiology behind this condition, what the latest scientific research reveals, and the symptoms you should never ignore. You'll also learn how GLP-1 medications influence appetite, insulin secretion, blood sugar regulation, and gastric emptying, along with important potential side effects involving the stomach, gallbladder, pancreas, and kidneys. These medications have demonstrated significant benefits for many patients, but understanding their possible risks is essential for making informed healthcare decisions. Sudden blurred vision, missing areas of vision, or sudden vision loss require immediate emergency medical attention. Severe or persistent abdominal pain also deserves prompt evaluation. Do not discontinue prescribed medications without speaking with your healthcare professional. Understanding what's happening inside your body can help you recognize warning signs, protect your health, and make better decisions for your future. Scientific research and the official FDA safety communication are provided below for educational reference.

SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH & FDA SAFETY COMMUNICATION

1. U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) — November 9, 2026

FDA Requires Safety Labeling Changes for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Due to Potential Increased Risk of Rare But Serious Eye Condition (NAION).

FDA analysis of 126 randomized clinical trials found 6.4 cases of NAION per 100,000 person-years among GLP-1 users compared with 3.8 cases in comparison groups.

Official FDA Safety Communication:
https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requires-safety-labeling-changes-glucagon-peptide-1-receptor-agonists-glp-1-ras-due-potential

2. Hathaway JT, et al. — JAMA Ophthalmology (2024)

Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy in Patients Prescribed Semaglutide.

Research identifying an association between semaglutide use and increased NAION risk in patients with diabetes or overweight/obesity.

PubMed PMID: 38958939
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38958939/

3. Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (2026)

Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.

Analysis of multiple studies examining the relationship between GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, and NAION risk.

PubMed PMID: 42060879
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42060879/

4. American Academy of Ophthalmology & North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society (2026)

Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Non-Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy: A Consensus Statement.

Clinical guidance reviewing the evidence, potential risks, and considerations for patients taking GLP-1 medications.

PubMed PMID: 42132708
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42132708/

Important: These findings concern a potential association between GLP-1 medications and NAION. The complication remains rare, and the available research does not establish that these medications directly cause NAION in every reported case.

***********************************

videos.title: Tom Watson Watches His First Major Win, 51 YEARS LATER
videos.summary_source_text:
Tom Watson Watches His First Major Win, 51 YEARS LATER SUBSCRIBE -  https://bit.ly/RandaGolfSubscribe

Tom Watson sits down to watch back his first major win, 51 years on, at Carnoustie in 1975: his first ever Open.

On his debut in the Championship, a 25-year-old Watson holed a 20-foot birdie putt on the 72nd hole to tie Jack Newton. That forced an 18-hole Monday playoff, the last one ever played at The Open. Watson won it by a single stroke to lift the Claret Jug, the first of his eight major titles.

videos.title: Elon Musk's Macrohard: The AI That Could Run An Entire Company!
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk's Macrohard: The AI That Could Run An Entire Company! Elon Musk wants to build an AI company that can replace Microsoft without hiring a single human employee. He's calling it Macrohard. And behind that joke name are a $60 billion Cursor acquisition agreement, a $2 billion Tesla investment, a $1.25 trillion SpaceX-xAI deal, and one enormous unanswered question: Where is the working product?

More than a year after Musk first announced Macrohard, there's still no independently verified public demonstration of it building and shipping software autonomously. No confirmed customers. No pricing. No published reliability benchmarks.

And the story gets even stranger when you look at what reportedly happened inside xAI before Musk unveiled Macrohard as a joint Tesla and xAI project.

On August 22, 2025, Musk announced his vision for a purely AI software company. But xAI had reportedly filed the Macrohard trademark 21 days earlier. This wasn't just a joke on X. There was real corporate activity behind it.

Then, in March 2026, Musk introduced a new architecture involving Grok and Digital Optimus.

Grok would act as the planner, directing complex tasks and coordinating the bigger picture. Tesla's Digital Optimus would serve as the computer-operating agent, using live screen video, keyboard inputs, and mouse movements to interact with software.

Musk compared the arrangement to the human brain's System 1 and System 2: one component acts, while the other thinks.

The ambition goes far beyond AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot or Cursor. Macrohard is supposed to simulate an entire software organization, potentially handling development, testing, deployment, management, and other business operations with minimal human involvement.

But there's a complication.

Business Insider reported that the original Macrohard project had stalled inside xAI amid management restructuring and the suspension of a data project involving roughly 600 outside workers. Meanwhile, Tesla's Digital Optimus effort was reportedly gaining momentum.

Was the March announcement a genuine breakthrough, or a restructuring of two separate AI projects?

Then there's the money.

Tesla approved approximately $2 billion to invest in xAI. SpaceX acquired xAI in an all-stock transaction that Reuters valued at approximately $1.25 trillion for the combined company. And in June 2026, SpaceX signed an agreement to acquire Cursor's parent company, Anysphere, in an all-stock deal implying a $60 billion valuation.

Cursor had been valued at $29.3 billion just seven months earlier.

Microsoft reportedly considered acquiring Cursor but never submitted a formal bid. Now Musk has agreed to pay roughly twice Cursor's previous valuation while pursuing an AI system named after Microsoft's opposite.

But there's an important distinction: No public confirmation establishes that Cursor will become part of Macrohard.

And the technical challenges are enormous.

Consider a hypothetical AI agent that completes each individual action with 99% accuracy. Across 50 independent steps, the probability of completing everything correctly falls to roughly 60%. At 95% per-step accuracy, that drops to about 8%.

Now imagine coordinating thousands of actions across an entire software company.

That raises serious questions about reliability, persistent memory, hallucinations, prompt injection attacks, security, operating costs, and accountability.

In this video, we examine what Musk has actually announced, what independent reporting supports, and what remains speculation.

We also explore why Tesla shareholders are paying attention, how Macrohard compares with Microsoft's Copilot strategy and competing AI agents from Anthropic and Google, and what this could mean for developers, software companies, and businesses investing in AI automation.

Musk has access to enormous capital, AI research, custom Tesla chips, and computing infrastructure. But can those resources solve the reliability problems that still limit autonomous AI agents?

The real test isn't another announcement, acquisition, or ambitious prediction.

It's whether Macrohard can demonstrate a complete, useful workflow without a human stepping in to fix the mistakes.

Until then, is Macrohard the beginning of a fully autonomous software company, or a multibillion-dollar vision running ahead of the technology?

The guys then turn their attention to the New Jersey Devils, breaking down the team's improved depth, Connor Brown's impressive contributions, and whether Timo Meier is doing enough to justify his role. Hashimoto’s disease is the most common cause of hypothyroidism, accounting for around 90% of underactive thyroid cases.

Hashimoto’s is an autoimmune condition in which antibodies attack the thyroid gland. It’s very common, affecting roughly 1 in 10 people, and is far more common in women than men.

Many people with Hashimoto’s may not notice symptoms at first. Others may experience weight gain, dry hair, high cholesterol, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping.

In some cases, taking iodine may actually worsen symptoms. Many people with Hashimoto's who are taking synthetic thyroid hormones still struggle to feel better because the underlying autoimmune component is not being addressed.

Vitamin D plays an important role in thyroid health and function. Vitamin K2 and magnesium are important cofactors that support vitamin D function and absorption.

Most of the gluten people consume today comes from modern wheat, which contributes to inflammation and negatively affects thyroid health for many people. Genetic factors can also increase susceptibility to autoimmune conditions.

Selenium, zinc, and magnesium are essential trace minerals for a healthy thyroid and play a key role in converting T4 into the active thyroid hormone T3.

Modern wheat is also commonly sprayed with glyphosate. Although it’s considered “safe,” the long-term effects of this herbicide on thyroid health remain unclear.

Vitamin D can help support immune balance and reduce inflammation, which can be beneficial for people dealing with autoimmune disease.

"I Nearly Walked Away From It All" | Dan Brown Reveals All Dan Brown joins George Harper Jr. on the Life on Tour podcast, presented by Buffalo Trace, at The Belfry ahead of the 2026 Husqvarna British Masters earlier this season. Dan reflects on his remarkable journey through professional golf, from coming close to walking away from the game in his early years as a professional to fulfilling his ambition of reaching the PGA Tour.

Industrin befinner sig i ett skifte där fysisk AI, robotik och autonoma system skapar nya möjligheter att effektivisera arbetet och minska den fysiska belastningen i produktionen. Samtidigt handlar omställningen inte bara om vilken teknik vi kan införa, utan hur vi får människor och teknik att utvecklas tillsammans.

videos.title: 19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: BOUNCE-BACK: Colorado Avalanche DOMINATE Ducks as Wedgewood, Nelson and T.J. Hughes Impress
videos.summary_source_text:
BOUNCE-BACK: Colorado Avalanche DOMINATE Ducks as Wedgewood, Nelson and T.J. Hughes Impress Colorado Avalanche blank Anaheim Ducks behind Scott Wedgewood’s clutch shutout and an offensive surge led by Brock Nelson. Can the Avs maintain consistency and seize momentum with stars Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon sidelined?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down Colorado’s dominant 4-0 bounce-back win, spotlighting T.J. Hughes’ poise and playmaking, Devon Toews’ impressive offensive turnaround, and critical shifts in faceoff wins and special teams. The conversation explores key moments from Parker Kelly’s relentless forecheck to Adam Beckman’s physical debut, as well as the Avs’ defensive commitment against the Ducks’ top-ranked power play. Listeners get insights into the team’s resilience, evolving chemistry, and the puzzling up-and-down nature of recent performances.

Will this Avs squad finally find their groove with five days to reset, or are more rollercoaster nights ahead? Don’t miss the analysis and passionate fan reactions that sum up Colorado’s quest for consistency.

Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 19.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Linux vs. Windows 11 Battery Test (Lab Tested)
videos.summary_source_text:
Linux vs. Windows 11 Battery Test (Lab Tested) Sponsored by Wispr Flow! Wispr Flow Notetaker is free and now available on iPhone! Download today and get 1 month of Wispr Flow Pro with unlimited meetings in Notetaker plus unlimited words in Wispr Flow: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/phonebuff-yt-9

Battery test between Linux (Fedora) and Windows 11 to see which one is more efficient in real-world apps and workflows. We used two identically configured Dell XPS 13s (Intel Core 5 320, 8 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD).

TEST NOTES:

- Screens were calibrated to 200 nits with auto brightness turned off.
- Speakers calibrated to the nearest decibel count.
- Tested within equal distance of a WiFi access point.
- Tested in a temperature-controlled environment.
- Both laptops were set to their respective Balanced power profiles.
- Results ending at “shutdown” were based on each operating system’s automatic behavior.
- On Fedora, we installed RPM Fusion’s full-codec Intel VA-API media driver, adding hardware-accelerated H.264 and HEVC support omitted from Fedora’s stock driver.
- Fedora’s speaker-amplifier configuration was manually corrected because the XPS 13’s amplifiers were not properly enabled out of the box.
- Minecraft was capped to 30 FPS. Both laptops were able to well exceed this, but we kept it low to guarantee a performance match. 
- The tests used two identically configured but physically separate laptops. Small differences in battery capacity, silicon quality, cooling, or manufacturing could affect the results.

We Asked 4,000 Golfers Which Premium Ball They Play. It’s Closer Than You Think Which premium golf ball are golfers actually playing? More than 4,000 MyGolfSpy readers answered our 2026 Golf Ball Survey, and 3,119 of them play a urethane-cover ball. The Titleist Pro V1 leads at 13.0%, but the Maxfli Tour X is only 0.8 points behind at 12.2%. Titleist has more players overall, but Maxfli's strength is concentrated in one ball. And the fifth most-played urethane ball isn't even made by a golf company.

These results reflect MyGolfSpy survey respondents, not all golfers.

videos.summary_source_text:
PGA Tour Highlights | Round 1 | The RSM Classic | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 1 of the 2026 The RSM Classic, featuring Max Greyserman, Michael Thorbjornsen and Jackson Koivun, among others.

The PGA Tour season reaches its conclusion this week at The RSM Classic, with plenty at stake at Sea Island as players make their final push for 2027 status. Only the top 100 in the FedExCup Fall standings will secure full playing privileges, leaving several notable names under pressure. Billy Horschel sits just outside the line at No. 101, while Joel Dahmen, Luke Clanton and Haotong Li face a steep climb from further back. Peter Malnati has an even tougher task at No. 151, knowing only a victory can take him into the top 100. Sami Valimaki returns to defend his title, while five-time major champion Brooks Koepka makes his tournament debut. The Aon Next 10 is also up for grabs, with places 51-60 earning starts in the first two Signature Events of 2027. The lineup also includes the in-form Andrew Novak, Austin Smotherman and Blades Brown as well as Major Champion Brian Harman, the field is stacked and it is set to be a thrilling finale.

videos.title: How to Become Rich in Ways You Never Imagined | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text: How to Become Rich in Ways You Never Imagined | Dr. Mandell What if everything you thought you knew about being rich was wrong? We spend so much of our lives chasing money, success, and possessions, believing that one day they will bring us true happiness. But the greatest riches in life cannot be bought, borrowed, or replaced. True wealth is found in the love we share, the family and friends who stand beside us, the health we often take for granted, the memories we create, and the precious moments that make life meaningful. Sometimes we become so focused on what we don't have that we forget how blessed we already are. In this heartfelt and inspiring message, Dr. Alan Mandell reminds us that the richest people aren't necessarily those who have the most money, but those who recognize the priceless gifts already surrounding them. Take a moment to reflect, appreciate the people you love, and remember that time is one treasure we can never get back. If this message touches your heart, share it with someone you love. videos.title: Gemini 4 Neon Is Here: Google’s Powerful Model Just Beat GPT-6.2 Astra!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 Neon Is Here: Google’s Powerful Model Just Beat GPT-6.2 Astra! Google just released Gemini 4 Neon, only six days after Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Independent benchmarks place it among the world's most intelligent AI models, delivering nearly twice Carbon's output speed at a significantly lower cost per task. But one sentence buried inside Google's model card changes how you should look at this release.

Gemini 4 Neon is officially described as "adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon." No disclosed new architecture, no parameter count, and no confirmed training breakthrough. So is Neon genuinely a next-generation AI model, or an exceptionally well-optimized version of Carbon?

Google has now released four Gemini 4 models in just seven weeks: Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen, and Neon. The latest release also arrived just one day after OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol into its API.

In this video, we break down Gemini 4 Neon's independent benchmarks, real-world capabilities, reasoning performance, pricing, spectacular launch demos, technical limitations, and the important details Google buried in its benchmark footnotes.

Artificial Analysis ranked Gemini 4 Neon third overall on its Intelligence Index at its highest reasoning setting, behind GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2. Neon scored 61 compared to Carbon's 60, while delivering approximately 110 tokens per second against Carbon's 57.

Vals AI also ranked Neon second out of 42 models, with particularly strong performance in finance and legal tasks. Independent evaluations suggest that Google's biggest achievement isn't necessarily higher intelligence — it's making near-frontier intelligence faster and cheaper.

But Google's own benchmarks deserve closer examination.

On SWE-sweep, Neon achieved an impressive 39.0 using Google's Antigravity CLI, compared to Claude Opus 5.5's 10.1 and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3. Switch to a neutral testing harness, however, and the competitive advantage changes dramatically. We examine why agent infrastructure, subagents, tool access, and execution environments matter just as much as the underlying model.

Then there are Google's spectacular demonstrations:

- A realistic Mont Blanc skiing simulator with approximately 10,200 lines of custom shader code.
- A spreadsheet-based photo editor using roughly 100,000 cells and over 500,000 formulas.
- A reconstruction of Alan Turing's 1936 study with a working Universal Turing Machine.
- A Blender-generated laboratory environment using MCP integration.
- A multi-agent game built using Antigravity's /swarm command.

These demonstrations showcase impressive coding, planning, and tool orchestration capabilities. However, they haven't been independently reproduced, and Neon itself remains a text-output model rather than a native 3D generator.

We also investigate why Neon's highest thinking level isn't necessarily its best. Going from high to xhigh reasoning delivers only one additional Intelligence Index point while adding nearly seven minutes of average task time. On one visual benchmark, performance actually declines.

Gemini 4 Neon supports a massive 1,048,576-token context window, multimodal inputs, up to 3,000 images, 3,000-page documents, and approximately 8.4 hours of audio. But documented capacity and demonstrated reliability are two very different things.

At $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, Neon sits between GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 in standard API pricing, while remaining significantly cheaper than GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2.

We break down the hidden costs of thinking tokens, context caching, search grounding, Antigravity's context limitations, and the difference between price per token and price per completed task.

Perhaps the biggest unanswered question, however, is safety.

Google has not yet published Neon's full Safety and Security Report. Some evaluations were inherited from Gemini 4 Argon, while hallucinations, jailbreak resistance, prompt injection, and agent security remain important considerations for developers and enterprises.

Is Gemini 4 Neon the best practical AI model for developers, coding agents, automation builders, and professional workloads? Or are Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic increasingly competing through efficiency and agent infrastructure rather than fundamental intelligence breakthroughs?

Watch the full breakdown before deciding which AI model deserves your money.

Independent benchmarks place it among the world's most intelligent AI models, delivering nearly twice Carbon's output speed at a significantly lower cost per task. But one sentence buried inside Google's model card changes how you should look at this release.

Gemini 4 Neon is officially described as "adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon." No disclosed new architecture, no parameter count, and no confirmed training breakthrough. So is Neon genuinely a next-generation AI model, or an exceptionally well-optimized version of Carbon?

Google has now released four Gemini 4 models in just seven weeks: Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen, and Neon. The latest release also arrived just one day after OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol into its API.

In this video, we break down Gemini 4 Neon's independent benchmarks, real-world capabilities, reasoning performance, pricing, spectacular launch demos, technical limitations, and the important details Google buried in its benchmark footnotes.

Artificial Analysis ranked Gemini 4 Neon third overall on its Intelligence Index at its highest reasoning setting, behind GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2. Neon scored 61 compared to Carbon's 60, while delivering approximately 110 tokens per second against Carbon's 57.

Vals AI also ranked Neon second out of 42 models, with particularly strong performance in finance and legal tasks. Independent evaluations suggest that Google's biggest achievement isn't necessarily higher intelligence — it's making near-frontier intelligence faster and cheaper.

But Google's own benchmarks deserve closer examination.

On SWE-sweep, Neon achieved an impressive 39.0 using Google's Antigravity CLI, compared to Claude Opus 5.5's 10.1 and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3. Switch to a neutral testing harness, however, and the competitive advantage changes dramatically. We examine why agent infrastructure, subagents, tool access, and execution environments matter just as much as the underlying model.

Then there are Google's spectacular demonstrations:

- A realistic Mont Blanc skiing simulator with approximately 10,200 lines of custom shader code.
- A spreadsheet-based photo editor using roughly 100,000 cells and over 500,000 formulas.
- A reconstruction of Alan Turing's 1936 study with a working Universal Turing Machine.
- A Blender-generated laboratory environment using MCP integration.
- A multi-agent game built using Antigravity's /swarm command.

These demonstrations showcase impressive coding, planning, and tool orchestration capabilities. However, they haven't been independently reproduced, and Neon itself remains a text-output model rather than a native 3D generator.

We also investigate why Neon's highest thinking level isn't necessarily its best. Going from high to xhigh reasoning delivers only one additional Intelligence Index point while adding nearly seven minutes of average task time. On one visual benchmark, performance actually declines.

Gemini 4 Neon supports a massive 1,048,576-token context window, multimodal inputs, up to 3,000 images, 3,000-page documents, and approximately 8.4 hours of audio. But documented capacity and demonstrated reliability are two very different things.

At $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, Neon sits between GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 in standard API pricing, while remaining significantly cheaper than GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2.

We break down the hidden costs of thinking tokens, context caching, search grounding, Antigravity's context limitations, and the difference between price per token and price per completed task.

Perhaps the biggest unanswered question, however, is safety.

Google has not yet published Neon's full Safety and Security Report. Some evaluations were inherited from Gemini 4 Argon, while hallucinations, jailbreak resistance, prompt injection, and agent security remain important considerations for developers and enterprises.

Is Gemini 4 Neon the best practical AI model for developers, coding agents, automation builders, and professional workloads? Or are Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic increasingly competing through efficiency and agent infrastructure rather than fundamental intelligence breakthroughs?

How to Target Your Lower Abs (GET A FLATTER STOMACH) Get a flat stomach here - https://athleanx.com/flatstomach

If you want more visible lower abs, pay attention to what happens *after* you bring your knees up. Can you curl your pelvis toward your chest, or do your legs move while your tailbone stays on the floor? That last part of the rep is easy to miss, and it can change how much work your abs actually do. In this video, I’m going to show you three lower ab exercises you can do at home, plus a bonus exercise for the pull-up bar. I’ll also cover where nutrition comes in if lower belly fat is hiding the muscle you’re working to build.

Can you target your lower abs? Your upper and lower abs are part of the same muscle, so both contribute when you do a crunch or a reverse crunch. You can, however, change the emphasis by changing which end of the movement you initiate from. In a standard crunch, you lift your shoulder blades off the floor and bring your rib cage toward your pelvis. To put more emphasis on the lower abs, work from the bottom up and bring your pelvis toward your rib cage.

You can feel the difference before you even start your first set. Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees. Now tip your belt buckle toward your chest until the gap underneath your low back closes. That’s a posterior pelvic tilt. From here, see if you can lift your tailbone an inch off the floor while keeping the bend in your hips and knees. It’s a small movement, but it’s the one I want you to recognize in each of the exercises that follows.

You can use that same setup to adjust the difficulty. Bring your thighs a little closer to your chest for an easier rep, or start with them farther away to make it harder. Once you pick an angle, hold it as you curl up. If your knees travel several inches before your tailbone starts to move, bring your thighs a little closer and try again.

First up are swipers. Start on your back with your legs raised and your hands beside your hips. Curl your pelvis up until you have enough room to swipe your hands together underneath your butt. What I like about this lower ab exercise is that every rep gives you feedback. If your feet went higher but your hands still hit the floor on either side of your hips, you know exactly what was missing. Reset, tuck your pelvis and lift again.

Next is the reverse knee tuck, an exercise I’d actually call a tailbone lift. Tell someone to tuck their knees and they can pull them all the way toward their abdomen while their pelvis barely moves. On your next rep, keep the bend in your knees and think about peeling your tailbone off the ground. Your knees will travel toward forehead level as your hips roll up. Lower yourself slowly enough to feel your pelvis return to the floor before you start the next rep.

The third exercise is the plank knee slide. This is where you take that same pelvic curl and use it in a plank. As you draw one knee forward, tuck your pelvis underneath you. It’s easy to rush through these and turn them into mountain climbers, so take your time on the way in and on the way back. If your low back sags as you extend your leg, reset your plank before you switch sides.

For a bonus, grab a pull-up bar and try the hanging leg raise. Here’s my favorite cue for this one. Imagine you’re trying to show your butt to the person standing in front of you. You can raise your thighs to waist height and still have your belt buckle pointing straight ahead. Curl your pelvis forward and watch where that belt buckle goes. Your hip flexors help lift your legs, and your abs do the work of curling your pelvis up against gravity. Control the descent so you can start the next rep without swinging.

Want to make these lower ab exercises harder? On swipers, reverse knee tucks and hanging leg raises, cross your legs and squeeze them together to engage your inner thighs. On plank knee slides, press your planted foot into the floor and imagine dragging it inward without letting it move. You can also add a small amount of rotation by curling one side of your pelvis toward the opposite side of your rib cage.

If your goal is a more visible six pack, your nutrition needs to support overall fat loss. That means maintaining a calorie deficit over time while you continue to train.

videos.title: Skånsk äggakaka på stekhäll #350 I Kapten Mat
videos.summary_source_text:
Skånsk äggakaka på stekhäll #350 I Kapten Mat Kaptenens gourmethelg på Wisingsö Hotell bokar du här: 
https://boka.wisingso.se/package/package-details?channelid=dae7aa86-a151-492a-9b7d-38a6c2e046e5&packageid=9690cf56-227b-44db-ad2a-e7fb3f7bdffd

Skånsk äggakaka med rökt sidfläsk och lingonsylt
6 portioner · ca 50 min

ÄGGAKAKAN
10 ägg
3,5 dl vetemjöl
2 tsk salt
1 l mjölk
75 g smör

FLÄSKET
400–800 g rökt sidfläsk i ca 1 cm tjocka skivor

LINGONSYLTEN
225 g lingon, färska eller frysta
1,25 dl strösocker (ca 110 g)
0,5 dl vatten
4 cl eau-de-vie

GÖR SÅ HÄR:
Lingonsylten: Koka upp lingon och vatten i en kastrull. Rör ner sockret och låt sylten sjuda på medelvärme i ca 8–10 min. Rör om då och då. Skumma av ytan och dra kastrullen från värmen. Rör ner eau-de-vien och låt sylten svalna. Den tjocknar när den kallnar.

Smeten: Börja med att vispa äggen. Vispa sedan i mjöl och salt. Vispa i hälften av mjölken och sedan resten. Låt smeten vila i en kvart.

Fläsket: Stek fläsket på medelvärme i stekhällen tills det är knaprigt. Lyft upp det och håll det varmt. Låt allt flott ligga kvar i hällen och lägg i smöret och låt det smälta.

Stek första sidan: Rör om smeten och häll den i hällen. Sänk till låg värme. Skrapa med spackelspaden från kanterna in mot mitten. Låt kakan stelna utan lock i ca 15–20 min samtidigt som du skrapar. Kanterna ska släppa och ytan nästan ha stelnat.

Vänd: När kakan har stelnat vänder du den med hjälp av en pizzaspade.
Stek klart under lock i ytterligare 5-10 min.

Servera: Lägg tillbaka fläsket ovanpå äggakakan och servera direkt från hällen med lingonsylten.

Låg värme är det viktigaste. Är värmen för hög blir botten bränd innan kakan har stelnat.

400–800 g rökt sidfläsk i ca 1 cm tjocka skivor
