Did this Luxury Chinese SUV just KILL the UK car industry? Is a £57,000 Chinese SUV more luxurious than a £200,000 Range Rover SV?! 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow 

Introducing the Li Auto L9 Livis! It’s an all-new luxurious SUV that is set to go on sale in the UK next year. 

It’s packed full of tech and luxurious features, and it clearly has class leaders such as the Range Rover in its sights! The question is, does it have what it takes to go toe-to-toe with a brand as renowned as Range Rover? 

To find out, Mat’s brought the two of them together to see just how they compare. So let’s take a closer look at the L9, starting with the design! 

Up top, the first thing you’ll notice is the huge swooping DRL that runs across the front of the car. Below this sit a pair of matrix LED headlights, and there are panels in the centre of the bumper that open up to assist with airflow. Along the side, the two-tone paint job helps give the car more presence, and there are a host of cameras and sensors on the car to assist with autonomous driving and parking. The side view also highlights just how big the car is, stretching to 5.2m long! Around the back, there’s a taillight that stretches across the length of the car, but otherwise it’s a relatively plain rear end. 

While the exterior may have been relatively plain, the interior comes absolutely packed with features. At the front, there’s a huge infotainment screen stretching across the length of the dash, and there’s Nappa leather on the steering wheel and seats. In fact, every surface you touch in the front is covered in soft-touch materials! 

The L9 is a six-seater, so step into the back, and you’ll find a pair of Captain’s chairs! They’re full of adjustments and massage functions, and there’s a retractable touchscreen that drops down from the roof, similar to what you’ll find in a BMW 7 Series. There’s also a fridge, blinds for the windows, and the third row of seats also comes with the ability to recline. There’s no denying it’s one luxurious interior! 

Under the bonnet? Well, in comparison to the Range Rover’s V8, here you’ll only find a 1.5-litre turbo petrol. However, this isn’t the L9’s main power source - it’s used as a generator to power two electric motors, and these combine to produce 571hp and 710Nm! 

The L9 Livis only costs around £57,000 in China, so it’s around a quarter of the price of the Range Rover SV! The question is, if you’re in the market for a luxurious SUV, would you be willing to choose a new Chinese entrant over an established brand like Range Rover? Let us know in the comments!

The L9 Livis only costs around £57,000 in China, so it’s around a quarter of the price of the Range Rover SV! The question is, if you’re in the market for a luxurious SUV, would you be willing to choose a new Chinese entrant over an established brand like Range Rover? Let us know in the comments!

videos.summary_source_text:
18.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After visiting 25 countries across five continents, the DP World Tour’s schedule reaches a climax this week in Dubai, for the DP World Tour Championship, marking the final event of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. Since 2009, the DP World Tour Championship has annually played host to the season-ending event. Contested over 72 holes, with no cut, the final Rolex Series event features a $10 million prize fund, the biggest of the 2026 Race to Dubai season. 50 players have made their way to the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events, which form the DP World Tour Play-offs. videos.title: Hindi - 18.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 18.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Eat Cottage Cheese Before Bed — Here's What Happens to Your Body!  Dr. Mandell What really happens inside your body when you eat cottage cheese before bed? This simple, protein-rich food contains casein, a slow-digesting protein that gradually releases amino acids into your bloodstream throughout the night, helping support muscle protein synthesis and overnight recovery. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the fascinating physiology behind casein, why preserving muscle mass becomes increasingly important after age 40, and how adequate protein supports strength, mobility, and healthy aging. Discover how cottage cheese provides important nutrients for bone health, helps satisfy nighttime hunger, and makes a nutritious alternative to sugary evening snacks. We'll also explore the relationship between muscle mass, glucose metabolism, and maintaining your independence as you age. Sometimes the simplest foods provide powerful nutritional benefits!

Scientific Research (PubMed):

Kouw et al. (2017). "Protein Ingestion before Sleep Increases Overnight Muscle Protein Synthesis Rates in Healthy Older Men: A Randomized Controlled Trial." PMID: 28855419.

Holwerda et al. (2016). "Physical Activity Performed in the Evening Increases the Overnight Muscle Protein Synthetic Response to Presleep Protein Ingestion in Older Men." PMID: 27281811.

"Effects of Pre-Sleep Protein Consumption on Muscle-Related Outcomes: A Systematic Review" (2020). PMID: 32811763.

"Pre-Sleep Protein in Casein Supplement or Whole-Food Form Has No Impact on Resting Energy Expenditure or Hunger in Women" (2018). PMID: 30249314.

videos.title: GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol Are Here — The Demos Are Insane
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol Are Here — The Demos Are Insane OpenAI just launched GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, skipping GPT-6.1 Astra entirely. The new flagship is 20% cheaper, supposedly beats Claude Fable 5.2 at a fraction of the cost, and has crossed OpenAI's "High" AI self-improvement threshold. But independent benchmarks tell a very different story.

Artificial Analysis scores GPT-6.2 Astra at 62, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65. Meanwhile, GPT-6.2 Sol delivers performance close to the previous flagship for a fraction of the cost. So is Astra really OpenAI's biggest breakthrough, or is the cheaper Sol actually the more important release?

On November 17, OpenAI introduced two new models with ambitious claims about coding, reasoning, research, engineering, cybersecurity, and cost efficiency. But once you separate OpenAI's internal benchmarks from independent testing, the picture gets much more complicated.

First, there's the showcase.

OpenAI demonstrated a playable 3D racing game called Meridian Sound Racing, reportedly generated by Astra. It also showcased a Marina City-inspired lamp designed through CAD, a Blender car simulation, an RC buggy assembly guide, financial models, and automated presentation workflows.

The racing game is publicly playable. Most of the other demonstrations aren't. OpenAI hasn't disclosed the complete prompts, failed attempts, human edits, or tool configurations behind these results. That leaves a critical question: how much of the impressive output comes from the AI model itself, and how much depends on the surrounding software and human guidance?

Then there's pricing.

GPT-6.2 Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, a 20% reduction from GPT-6 Astra. GPT-6.2 Sol stays at $2 input and $10 output, making Astra four times more expensive at standard token rates.

On a workload involving 10 million input tokens and 2 million output tokens per day, that's roughly $160 for Astra versus $40 for Sol. Over 30 days, the difference reaches approximately $3,600.

But cheaper tokens don't necessarily mean cheaper completed tasks.

OpenAI claims Astra beats Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 percentage points on Agents' Last Exam at approximately 5% of the estimated cost. Yet the comparison involves different reasoning configurations, different task counts, and estimated competitor costs.

Independent results complicate the story further. Artificial Analysis places Fable 5.2 ahead of Astra, while Epoch AI reports a tie on its broader Capabilities Index. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon also remains competitive.

And the coding results are especially interesting.

Despite OpenAI's claims about cleaner code and fewer revisions, Artificial Analysis found essentially no improvement in Astra's coding score over GPT-6 Astra. Sol's coding score actually declined on that index.

That doesn't mean the models haven't improved. It means efficiency, code quality, and correctness are different things.

The biggest practical development may actually be GPT-6.2 Sol.

Sol reaches an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 57, matching the previous GPT-6 Astra flagship. On Vals AI, Sol costs approximately $3.18 per task compared with Astra's $10.68, while their overall scores sit surprisingly close.

For developers, businesses, and anyone running AI automation at scale, that difference could matter more than another frontier-model benchmark victory.

Then there's OpenAI's most controversial claim: Astra is its first externally deployed model to reach the "High" threshold for AI self-improvement under its Preparedness framework.

Does that mean self-improving AI or AGI has arrived?

Not according to the available evidence. The threshold measures performance on internal research-engineering tasks, not autonomous self-retraining or independent recursive improvement. There's also no public independent audit confirming the result.

We also examine the missing information: unpublished context-window specifications, private legal-AI benchmarks, unverified demonstrations, hallucination rates, and the limits of current independent testing.

Ultimately, the real question isn't which model wins a carefully selected benchmark. It's which model delivers reliable, usable results at a price that makes sense.

Should you use GPT-6.2 Astra, switch to Sol, or stick with Claude Fable 5.2?

Watch the full breakdown before making that decision.

Which real-world task would you like to see Astra and Sol tested on side by side? Drop it in the comments.

videos.title: Steroids Work - But What's Really The Problem?
videos.summary_source_text:
Steroids Work - But What's Really The Problem? Steroids build muscle. Medicine argued about it for decades, until a 1996 trial settled it. The real question was always the bill.

In this investigation: what anabolic steroids are and how they work, where they came from (Vienna 1954, Dianabol, East Germany's State Plan 14.25, Ben Johnson), who uses them today, why "steroids" is a whole family of drugs, the black-market supply chain, and what the research shows about hormones and fertility, the heart, the liver, the kidneys and the mind. Then six gym myths, and the line between supervised testosterone therapy after 40 and use without a doctor.

This is education, not a diagnosis. If you use anabolic steroids or are thinking about it, talk honestly with a doctor: blood tests and a heart check can show problems long before you feel them.

Pulls, fades, poor contact and drives that come up short often start with the left side of your body: a level setup, an all-arms backswing with no width, and a left shoulder that moves too far forward on the way down. That leaves you hitting down on the ball with no speed, a pattern Eric Cogorno sees often in golf lessons with players who struggle with driver. The fix comes from what Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy and Justin Thomas have in common: a setup with your left hip and left shoulder higher, width in the backswing, and a left shoulder that goes up and back on the downswing. Together, these golf swing tips give you the two things Eric says you need to hit driver farther, an upward angle of attack and more speed, and he shows how to adjust the downswing feel for pulls and fades or pushes and hooks. If you leave this video without trying the feel of punching the club away from you, you're leaving speed and distance on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• Why an all-arms backswing costs you width and speed
• How to set up with your left hip and left shoulder higher
• How to start the backswing with your left shoulder under your chin
• How to create width like Bryson DeChambeau
• How to feel width by punching the club away from you
• Why your left shoulder should go up and back, not forward, on the downswing
• How to fix pulls and fades, or pushes and hooks, with driver
• High handicap golf tips for golfers who struggle with driver

If Your Back or Hips Feel Tight When You Stand Up, Don't Just Stretch Them If your back or hips feel tight or sore when you stand up from a chair, join me for a gentle seated movement exploration.

We’ll explore small movements of the pelvis, circles, and comfortable diagonal reaching, noticing how your pelvis and spine move together. Then slowly stand up and sit down again, and notice whether anything feels different.

Grab a chair, keep the movements small, and adjust them to your comfort. There’s no need to force a stretch or reach farther.

If you'd like to explore this approach more deeply, I invite you to try my free guided movement masterclass—a chance to explore gentle movement and curiosity at your own pace:

videos.title: 17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
17.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

Learn. Participate. Manage Risk. Think Bigger.

videos.title: Do This 1 Thing to Your RICE… Less Sugar, Fewer Calories & a Healthier Gut!  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Do This 1 Thing to Your RICE… Less Sugar, Fewer Calories & a Healthier Gut!  Dr. Mandell What if one simple change to the way you prepare rice could help your body digest fewer starches, support healthier blood sugar levels, and improve your gut health? When you cook rice and refrigerate it, something fascinating happens! A portion of the starch undergoes a natural process called retrogradation, forming resistant starch that is harder for your body to digest. Instead of being rapidly broken down into glucose, some of this resistant starch travels to your colon, where beneficial gut bacteria ferment it and produce short-chain fatty acids, including butyrate. Butyrate helps nourish the cells lining your colon, supports intestinal health, and plays an important role in maintaining a healthy gut environment. Research also suggests that cooling cooked rice can reduce its glycemic response under certain conditions, although results vary and the total carbohydrate content doesn't disappear. This fascinating process can also occur in potatoes and pasta, giving you a simple way to modify how your body processes some of your favorite starchy foods. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the science behind resistant starch, its relationship to blood sugar, insulin sensitivity, digestion, and gut bacteria, and how one easy preparation technique can make a difference in your everyday nutrition. Always refrigerate cooked rice promptly, keep it properly chilled, and reheat thoroughly when ready to eat. Wishing you great health! Dr. Mandell

Scientific Research (PubMed):

Sonia S et al. (2015). Effect of cooling of cooked white rice on resistant starch content and glycemic response. Asia Pacific Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

Birt DF et al. (2013). Resistant Starch: Promise for Improving Human Health. Advances in Nutrition. PMID: 24228189.

den Besten G et al. (2013). The role of short-chain fatty acids in the interplay between diet, gut microbiota, and host energy metabolism. Journal of Lipid Research. PMID: 23821742.

Butyrate helps nourish the cells lining your colon, supports intestinal health, and plays an important role in maintaining a healthy gut environment. Research also suggests that cooling cooked rice can reduce its glycemic response under certain conditions, although results vary and the total carbohydrate content doesn't disappear. This fascinating process can also occur in potatoes and pasta, giving you a simple way to modify how your body processes some of your favorite starchy foods. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the science behind resistant starch, its relationship to blood sugar, insulin sensitivity, digestion, and gut bacteria, and how one easy preparation technique can make a difference in your everyday nutrition. Always refrigerate cooked rice promptly, keep it properly chilled, and reheat thoroughly when ready to eat. Wishing you great health! Dr. Mandell

videos.title: Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This!
videos.summary_source_text:
Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This! Your wrists shouldn’t be the reason you cut your chest workout short. If you get wrist pain when doing a dumbbell bench press, take a look at how you’re gripping the weight.

The problem? Grabbing the dumbbell right in the middle and letting the thumb side of your hand drop can put your wrist in an uncomfortable position under load. Before you pick up another set, try making this small adjustment.

The fix is simple:
Shift your grip slightly toward the end of the handle and focus your squeeze through your ring and pinky fingers. This helps position the pinky side of your hand slightly higher than the thumb side.

In this video, I’ll show you why that small change matters using the bones of the wrist and forearm. Adjusting the angle of your hand changes how the weight loads the wrist and can help make your dumbbell pressing more comfortable.

Same exercise. Better grip.

videos.title: xAI's Grok 5 Is INSANE: Elon Musk's Plan to Reach AGI!
videos.summary_source_text:
xAI's Grok 5 Is INSANE: Elon Musk's Plan to Reach AGI! Elon Musk says Grok 5 has a 10% chance of becoming AGI and could be the smartest AI in the world across every metric. But there's one major problem: Grok 5 still hasn't launched, and none of those predictions comes with independently verified benchmarks.

Behind the hype is a massive AI infrastructure project: xAI's Colossus supercomputer in Memphis, reportedly approaching 440,000 GPUs, gigawatt-scale power requirements, and a federal legal battle over gas turbines. Musk has also reportedly discussed a six-trillion-parameter model capable of real-time video understanding and advanced autonomous agents.

But can more computing power actually deliver artificial general intelligence? And why do Grok 5's release deadlines keep slipping?

We trace five major Grok 5 promises, from Musk's September 2025 AGI prediction and 10% probability estimate to the shifting launch timeline that now places Grok 4.8 and Grok 4.9 ahead of Grok 5.

Then we examine what xAI has actually delivered. Grok 4.7 posted improvements in coding benchmarks, including 71.0% on DeepSWE 1.1, 46.3% on CursorBench 4.0, and 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 according to xAI. With pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, Grok has a compelling cost advantage.

However, independent comparisons tell a more complicated story. Grok 4.7 trails leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic on several evaluations, while Google's Gemini 4 Argon raises the competitive bar even further. We examine GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and the benchmark differences that marketing headlines often overlook.

And there's a revealing twist: shortly before Grok 4.7 launched, Musk himself suggested it would be closer to an older Claude Opus model, while positioning Grok 4.9 as the potential competitor to newer frontier systems. That puts his extraordinary Grok 5 predictions into perspective.

We also investigate Colossus 2, reports of a possible 1.1-million-GPU expansion, the NAACP's environmental challenge, and the Justice Department's national-security argument. Plus, we separate existing Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and Grok Build capabilities from the much harder promises of unified real-time video reasoning and long-running autonomous agents.

Finally, we examine the AGI question itself. What would Grok 5 need to demonstrate on independent tests like ARC-AGI and Humanity's Last Exam? Can it handle multi-day projects without supervision? And how would xAI address safety, misinformation, and adversarial content risks inherited from earlier Grok releases?

Three outcomes remain possible: a genuine breakthrough, a strong but incremental frontier model, or another release that falls short of enormous expectations.

The real test won't be Musk's next prediction. It will be what independent evaluators discover after Grok 5 actually ships.

Subscribe to BitBiased for independent AI analysis, benchmark comparisons, and the technology stories behind the headlines.

videos.title: Every Shot Of Jon Rahm's Final Winning Round | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship
videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot Of Jon Rahm's Final Winning Round | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship Every shot from Jon Rahm's final round at the 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship where he secured his record winning SIXTH Rolex Series victory on the DP World Tour, taking down Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather than the hunted. Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. The 70 player field is stacked with star-studded names, featuring 6 major winners including Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Patrick Reed alongside three-time season winner Eugenio Chacarra who will be hoping to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. With enhanced points on offer it also means that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over.

videos.summary_source_text:
Where is Jensen Huang's Girlfriend?! Who is Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving NVIDIA and Jensen Huang? From her early career in Chinese television and finance to her reported relationship with NVIDIA's CEO and her current whereabouts, this documentary investigates everything we know about Alice Huang.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, has become one of the most controversial figures in the NVIDIA story. US officials reportedly suspect her of having connections to Chinese intelligence. But how much of the story is supported by evidence, and how much remains unverified?

In this documentary, we investigate Alice Huang's biography, her reported work at CCTV, HSBC, and CITIC Securities, her connection to Megaspeed International, and how she entered Jensen Huang's professional circle.

We also examine the reported affair involving Jensen Huang, his resignation, NVIDIA's response, the Singapore investigation, Taiwan's restrictions, and reports that Alice Huang is now living in Beijing.

Most importantly, we separate documented facts from intelligence allegations and unanswered questions.

**In this video:**
- Who is Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le?
- Her early life, career, and financial background
- How Megaspeed International connected her to NVIDIA
- How she reportedly met Jensen Huang
- The relationship and alleged Chinese intelligence connection
- What US officials have claimed about espionage
- What Singapore's investigation actually established
- Why Jensen Huang resigned from NVIDIA
- Where Alice Huang is reportedly living today
- What remains unknown about the alleged spy scandal

Watch the FULL video here: https://youtu.be/xyBOSZVKpNM

🌟 Take Dr. Berg’s New Health Quiz—60 seconds is all it takes:  https://www.drberg.com/lp/total-environments

Try avoiding food for at least 3 hours before bedtime. After dinner, mix 1 teaspoon of apple cider vinegar into a glass of water and drink it through a straw to help support more stable blood sugar throughout the night.

It’s time for an Audi vs Audi head-to-head!

The RS5 may be the newest car here, but it has one key difference to the RS6 GT - it’s powered by a V6 hybrid system, while the RS6 GT is packing a twin-turbo V8! But which will come out on top? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

This power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it’s significantly heavier than the RS6, tipping the scales at 2,355kg! videos.title: 16.11.26 - RIFT Training Day
videos.summary_source_text:
16.11.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Hindi - 16.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Eldrivna BMW M3 provkörd – jag körde originalet för 40 år sedan Läs hela testet på: https://alriksbilar.se/artiklar/bmw-m3-elektrisk/

För 40 år sedan var jag nyanställd på Teknikens Värld och skickades till Italien för att köra en väldigt speciell bil. Första BMW M3. 200 hästar, 1 200 kilo och sjukt kul.

Nu står jag på BMW:s testbana i Miramas med sjunde generationen. Den är eldriven. Fyra elmotorer, en per hjul. Batteri på 100 kWh, 420 kW snabbladdning och runt 650 kilometers räckvidd. Vikten? Den vill ingen på BMW säga ett ord om …

Jag åker först med Klaus Huber, chef för Driving Dynamics på BMW M. Sedan kör jag själv. Tre pass, det sista i regn. Jag testar låtsasväxlarna som BMW kallar stages, ljudet, sladdlägena och hur mycket bil man egentligen kan ställa om med några knapptryck. Johannes Bauer och Johannes Jurran förklarar tekniken bakom.

Så frågan. Är det här en äkta M3? Jag har kört alla generationer och jag har ett svar. Men vad tycker du? Skulle du ta den eldrivna eller vänta på bensinversionen? Skriv i kommentarerna!

Bilen är en kamouflerad prototyp, så allt är inte färdigt än.

- Improve her backswing and body movement
- Deliver the driver more efficiently
- Improve attack angle and launch
- Increase height and carry distance
- Produce a much more repeatable ball flight

videos.title: Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 KRYPTON Is INSANE — It Just Coded an Entire Game! Google's rumored Gemini 4 Krypton has sparked a massive question: did an unreleased AI model just prove it can build entire games? A leaked demo reportedly shows an eight-second anime-style animation generated entirely through code, taking 39 minutes and potentially involving nearly 247,000 tokens. But there's a major difference between generating impressive visuals and creating a playable game.

And that's where this story gets interesting.

On November 8, an X user known as Lyra claimed Google had developed an internal checkpoint called Krypton, reportedly outperforming Gemini 4 Carbon. Another developer, Chetaslua, shared comparisons involving a model labeled "krypton-a," including a detailed PlayStation 4 controller rendered in SVG and an anime-style floating island animation.

The numbers are striking. According to the reported comparison, Krypton used approximately 22,000 thinking tokens to generate the controller, versus 4,000 for Carbon. The anime animation reportedly ran for 39 minutes and 16 seconds at roughly 105 tokens per second.

But none of this has been independently verified. Google hasn't officially announced Gemini 4 Krypton, published its benchmarks, confirmed its specifications, or provided a release date.

So what can these leaked demonstrations actually tell us?

We examine the origins of the Krypton name, the reported visual comparisons, the quarter-million-token calculation, and why producing an animation isn't equivalent to building an interactive game with player controls, collision detection, physics, and functioning gameplay systems.

Then we compare those rumors with something Google has already demonstrated: four Gemini 4 Argon AI agents working together inside Minecraft.

According to published research, the agents defeated the Ender Dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs and dying 605 times along the way. Unlike a short visual demo, this experiment involved extended planning, execution, failure, and recovery. But the agents were playing Minecraft through a programming interface, not building the game itself.

Google's official AI lineup makes the story even more interesting.

Gemini 4 Carbon, announced October 28 and expanded to more users November 10, focuses on difficult, long-horizon reasoning, software engineering, debugging, and complex workflows.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen, officially introduced November 12, takes a different approach: faster coding and agentic execution. Google lists a one-million-token unified context window and pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Alongside Hydrogen, Google introduced Orchestrator in Antigravity, allowing different models to handle different parts of a development workflow. Google reports that Orchestrator achieved task success close to Carbon while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

But how does Google's AI actually compare against OpenAI and Anthropic?

We examine the reported benchmark results, including Carbon's Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 59, compared with Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57.

The competition becomes more complicated on coding benchmarks. Carbon reportedly scores 61.2% on FrontierSWE 2, behind GPT-6 Astra's 65.5%, while leading on the cited Terminal-Bench 4.0 comparison with 65.2%.

These are different evaluations measuring different capabilities. None proves an AI can independently produce a polished, enjoyable game.

We also explore what OpenAI Codex, Anthropic's coding agents, and xAI's Grok game-generation demonstrations reveal about the growing competition in AI-assisted software development.

For game developers, the bigger question isn't whether AI can generate thousands of lines of code. It's whether AI agents can build, test, debug, and improve working interactive experiences reliably.

So did Gemini 4 Krypton actually build a game? Is Google testing a breakthrough coding model, or are viral demos creating expectations that the evidence doesn't support?

The distinction matters more than ever.

videos.title: How To Avoid Losing Muscles After 40?
videos.summary_source_text:
How To Avoid Losing Muscles After 40? From your forties on, your body starts taking muscle from you, starting with your legs. It doesn't hurt and it gives no warning. Grip strength predicts the risk of dying better than blood pressure, yet fewer than 1 in 3 adults do the one thing that brings muscle back.

This documentary covers what the research shows about muscle loss after 40, why it matters, the 1990 Boston study that changed the field, and the three mistakes most people over 40 make.

Education, not a diagnosis. Talk to your doctor before starting a new training program.

videos.title: This Fixes 95% of Posture Problems (FAST!)
videos.summary_source_text:
This Fixes 95% of Posture Problems (FAST!) If you want to learn how to fix bad posture in 22 days, this step by step video gives you a plan for improving posture with stretches and strengthening exercises. Instead of guessing which posture exercises you need, I’m going to show you six simple tests you can perform at home to identify areas that need attention. Then, I’ll show you the stretches and exercises to address them and build your own posture correction routine.

Workouts, supplements, and mealplans here - http://athleanx.com
Subscribe to this channel here - http://youtube.com/user/jdcav24

The key to better posture is addressing your specific limitations consistently. This 22 day posture routine starts with testing your movement so you can focus on the areas that need work.

How to fix bad posture:

Day one starts with the posture test. As a physical therapist, I recommend seeing a qualified professional for an individual evaluation to understand your posture, the severity of any limitations and differences between your left and right sides. The six tests in this video give you a starting point for identifying areas to work on at home.

We’re looking at six areas: thoracic spine mobility, hamstring flexibility, calf flexibility, abdominal flexibility, hip flexor mobility and hip rotation. A rounded upper back, tight hamstrings, tight calves, tight abs, tight hip flexors and limited hip rotation can all affect how you move. Testing each area helps you decide which mobility exercises and stretches belong in your routine.

Each test uses a pass or fail approach. If you pass a test, you can skip the corresponding correction in this plan. If you fail a test, include the stretches and strengthening exercises shown for that area. This keeps your posture workout focused on your results instead of having you perform every exercise whether you need it or not.

After your initial assessment, alternate stretching days with exercise or strengthening days for the next 20 days. Follow the recommended hold times, sets and reps demonstrated in the video for each of your selected corrections. On day 22, repeat the original tests to see where your mobility and control have improved and what still needs attention.

For example, if your upper back is rounded and you struggle to extend through your thoracic spine, start with the kneeling thoracic extension stretch. Place your elbows on a surface in front of you, lower your chest and gently move your upper back into extension. The goal is to work on upper back mobility with control rather than force yourself into a position you cannot comfortably reach.

On your strengthening days, the face pull works the muscles of the upper back and shoulders. When you’re looking for exercises for rounded shoulders or ways to improve upper body posture, it’s easy to focus only on stretching. This routine pairs mobility work with strengthening so you also train the muscles that help you control your position.

The same approach applies to the other areas you test. Tight hip flexors, limited hip rotation or tight hamstrings may call for different corrections, which is why the assessment comes first. Use the demonstrations to choose your exercises for bad posture, and follow the instructions instead of adding random stretches to your day.

Improving posture takes consistency. You didn’t develop your everyday movement habits in a single day, and one posture stretch is not going to change everything overnight. Treat these 22 days as an opportunity to establish a repeatable routine, measure your progress and learn which areas deserve more attention.

You also don’t want to overdo the stretching. More force does not automatically mean better flexibility. Stay within a comfortable range, use controlled movement and avoid pushing through pain. The goal of these stretches for better posture is to gradually improve the movement you have available, not turn each session into a test of how much discomfort you can tolerate.

A useful posture correction routine combines flexibility, joint mobility and strength. Stretching addresses the restrictions identified by your tests, while the strengthening days help you practice controlling your movement. Keep following the schedule and use your final assessment to guide what you continue working on beyond day 22.

If you want to support better posture over the long term, complement this routine with a workout program that strengthens your entire body. The ATHLEAN-X programs combine strength training with attention to how you move. Head to athleanx.com and use the program selector to find the training plan that fits your goals.

For more videos on how to improve posture, stretches for tight muscles, upper back exercises and full body strength training, subscribe to the ATHLEAN-X YouTube channel. videos.title: The Reality of Reaching AGI
videos.summary_source_text:
The Reality of Reaching AGI Sam Altman says OpenAI will have an internal system it calls AGI by December 31, 2026. But does GPT-6 Astra actually meet OpenAI's own definition of artificial general intelligence? And with Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and xAI racing toward the same goal, which AI lab is genuinely closest?

Four CEOs have made four very different AGI predictions. Sam Altman has a deadline. Demis Hassabis sees AGI arriving within two to three years. Dario Amodei has put roughly 50/50 odds on a one-to-three-year timeline. And Elon Musk has reportedly suggested Grok 5 has around a 10% chance of achieving AGI.

But here's the problem: they aren't even using the same definition.

OpenAI's charter defines AGI as highly autonomous AI that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. Google DeepMind emphasizes the full cognitive range of the human brain. Anthropic focuses on transformative AI, while xAI sets its sights on answering fundamental questions about the universe.

So instead of trusting predictions, we're comparing the actual evidence.

Anthropic's newly released Fable 5.2 makes an even stronger case in some areas. It scores 74.6% on Terminal-Bench Science according to Anthropic, compared with Astra's 68.1%. Independent testing from Artificial Analysis puts Fable at 73%, supporting much of that result.

And then come Anthropic's extraordinary claims.

The company says approximately 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in just 30 hours. It reports AI-assisted advances in physics, protein design, and biological research. Anthropic also claims Claude now leads 26% of its internal AI research and development work.

But formalizing an existing proof isn't discovering new mathematics. Much of the scientific work still depends on human researchers, and several headline claims haven't been independently replicated.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon presents another challenge. Google's benchmarks show Argon winning 12 of 18 tests, including impressive results in video understanding and long-context reasoning. Yet limited availability makes broad independent verification difficult, and Google's comparisons predate Anthropic's latest release.

Meanwhile, Elon Musk's rumored AGI contender, Grok 5, hasn't launched. The available Grok 4.7 remains behind the leading models on independent intelligence rankings, despite xAI's enormous reported computing infrastructure.

But the biggest problem with every AGI prediction may be reliability.

METR's research estimates Anthropic's unreleased Mythos Preview can complete tasks requiring roughly 17.4 hours of human work at 50% success. Raise the reliability requirement to 80%, and that horizon drops to approximately three hours.

That's the difference between an impressive demonstration and an autonomous system you can actually depend on.

We also examine why AI benchmarks contradict each other, whether multi-agent systems are being mistaken for general intelligence, and why bigger GPU clusters alone may not determine the winner.

The missing pieces are substantial: reliable multi-day autonomy, continuous learning, long-term memory, real-world adaptability, and independently demonstrated recursive self-improvement.

So who leads the AGI race in late 2026?

Anthropic has compelling momentum in coding agents and AI-assisted science. OpenAI offers exceptional breadth in a publicly available flagship. Google leads in several multimodal and scientific areas. And xAI still has considerable ground to make up.

But none has publicly demonstrated AGI under OpenAI's own charter definition.

The real question isn't whether OpenAI can announce AGI before December 31. It's whether the company can provide evidence that independent researchers can actually verify.

Pulls, fades, poor contact and drives that come up short often start with the left side of your body: a level setup, an all-arms backswing with no width, and a left shoulder that moves too far forward on the way down. That leaves you hitting down on the ball with no speed, a pattern Eric Cogorno sees often in golf lessons with players who struggle with driver. The fix comes from what Tiger Woods, Rory McIlroy and Justin Thomas have in common: a setup with your left hip and left shoulder higher, width in the backswing, and a left shoulder that goes up and back on the downswing. Together, these golf swing tips give you the two things Eric says you need to hit driver farther, an upward angle of attack and more speed, and he shows how to adjust the downswing feel for pulls and fades or pushes and hooks. If you leave this video without trying the feel of punching the club away from you, you're leaving speed and distance on the table.

• Why an all-arms backswing costs you width and speed
• How to set up with your left hip and left shoulder higher
• How to start the backswing with your left shoulder under your chin
• How to create width like Bryson DeChambeau
• How to feel width by punching the club away from you
• Why your left shoulder should go up and back, not forward, on the downswing
• How to fix pulls and fades, or pushes and hooks, with driver
• High handicap golf tips for golfers who struggle with driver

videos.title: Avalanche Leave Montreal With a Solid Win in First Game Without MacKinnon and Makar
videos.summary_source_text:
Avalanche Leave Montreal With a Solid Win in First Game Without MacKinnon and Makar Colorado Avalanche shine without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar, toppling the Montreal Canadiens 4-1 on the road. Can the Avs maintain momentum despite missing two of their biggest stars?

The conversation focused on Mike Reilly’s arrival via waiver claim from the Carolina Hurricanes, bringing much-needed defensive depth as the Avalanche navigate their injury challenges. A key theme that emerged was Colorado’s balanced effort—Brock Nelson, Martin Nečas, Artturi Lehkonen, and others stepped up, with Mackenzie Blackwood delivering a standout .962 save percentage. The discussion explored the overturned high-stick goal, officiating transparency, and whether this gritty win signals sustained success or a brief spark. With special teams showing signs of improvement and upcoming matchups looming, can Colorado’s “next man up” mentality carry them through a tough stretch in the Western Conference?

videos.title: Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap!
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.8 Is Coming: Elon Musk 2.5 Trillion Parameter Massive Leap! Elon Musk says Grok 4.8 has 2.5 TRILLION parameters, making it xAI's biggest model yet. But here's the twist: Musk himself admits it isn't as good as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. And after a nearly two-month delay, xAI still hasn't published independent benchmark results to prove what its massive engineering overhaul actually achieved.

So why did xAI throw out its existing AI software stack and rebuild it from scratch in C and C++? And can a 100,000-GPU supercomputer help Grok close the gap with OpenAI and Anthropic?

The story behind Grok 4.8 is much bigger than another AI model release.

On November 10, Musk announced that Grok 4.8 had completed pre-training and entered reinforcement learning, with a limited rollout to Grok Bot users reportedly planned. But xAI hasn't published a Grok 4.8 model card, official benchmarks, API pricing, or a confirmed public release date.

That makes the 2.5-trillion-parameter claim particularly interesting. According to Musk's figures, Grok 4.8 is approximately 19% larger than Grok 4.7 and roughly 67% larger than Grok 4.6. But bigger models don't automatically deliver better intelligence.

And xAI's own Grok 4.7 benchmark chart reveals why.

On CursorBench 4.0, Grok 4.7 scored 46.3%, compared with 41.7% for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. That's impressive until you notice Claude Fable 5.1 scored 51.8%. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, the reported gap was even larger, with Grok around 38% against Fable's 58%.

These numbers matter because Grok 4.8 isn't competing against last year's AI models. It's entering a market already occupied by Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Google's Gemini lineup.

But the most unusual part of this story is what happened behind the scenes.

Musk says xAI abandoned JAX and SGLang in favor of custom C and C++ infrastructure for reinforcement learning and inference. He also says the Starlink software team developed an internal pre-training stack using low-level optimizations targeting Nvidia GPUs.

The potential advantage? Faster training, lower overhead, and more efficient use of expensive AI hardware.

The catch? Rebuilding critical infrastructure takes time, introduces engineering risks, and doesn't guarantee better model performance. Musk previously suggested the custom stack could deliver more than a tenfold training speedup on large runs, but that projection remains independently unverified.

Meanwhile, xAI's Colossus supercomputer in Memphis represents another extraordinary investment. Its original 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPU cluster was assembled in just 122 days, while Musk has described newer infrastructure targeting 220,000 Nvidia GB300 chips.

That's an enormous amount of compute behind a model that hasn't yet demonstrated its capabilities publicly.

We also examine what 2.5 trillion parameters actually means, why mixture-of-experts architectures complicate model-size comparisons, and why total parameter counts reveal surprisingly little about real-world coding, reasoning, and agent performance.

Then there's the business question.

Grok 4.7 offers API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, making it significantly cheaper on output than several frontier competitors. If Grok 4.8 delivers substantial improvements while preserving that advantage, xAI could become an increasingly attractive option for developers building AI agents.

But if the rewrite produces another delayed model that still trails Anthropic's best, the economics become harder to defend.

We break down the confirmed information, Musk's unverified claims, the overlooked benchmark results, the software rewrite, Colossus infrastructure, and what Grok 4.8 must accomplish to justify the investment.

The real question isn't whether xAI can build a bigger AI model.

It's whether all that hardware, custom software, and additional training can produce something meaningfully better.

Subscribe to BitBiased for analytical coverage of OpenAI, xAI, Anthropic, AI infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the technology shaping the future.
